content:
France's social security provides complete coverage for prenatal and postnatal medical expenses in public facilities. Working mothers receive 16 weeks of maternity leave with daily compensation between €9.29 ($10.94) and €84.90 ($100), depending on their previous earnings. During pregnancy and the period surrounding delivery, financial circumstances remain stable for families - those facing economic hardship continue to struggle at the same level as before, while affluent families maintain their comfortable status.

However, when it comes to practical support for new mothers, there's a significant gap in planning. Fathers receive just 11 days of paternity leave, insufficient time for mothers to physically recuperate from giving birth. Consequently, new mothers must handle constant infant care responsibilities while still recovering. They also face the challenge of finding childcare, particularly difficult in the Paris area where government-provided options fall short. Childcare expenses differ considerably. Public daycare centers offer affordable options at around €1,000 ($1,177.59) annually for lower-income families, but availability is extremely limited with only one spot per eight children. This shortage forces families to turn to private alternatives like individual childminders or in-home caregivers.

Any other questions?
